intro: Influencer marketing is booming, but most teams still run it like a messy side project. Too many profiles, too little signal, and a lot of money wasted on “reach” that does not convert.

sections.title: The Problem: Influencer Chaos
sections.content: The industry is growing fast, but for many companies it is still chaotic, time-consuming, and hard to measure. TheyTalk needed a brand and product presence that clearly explained the value of AI-driven matching, built trust with investors and partners, and felt native to the social media world influencers live in.

sections.title: The Challenge: Big Ambition, Start-Up Reality
sections.content: The founders wanted a strong identity and a demo-ready platform to pitch investors. Tight budget. Tighter deadline. We had to create something that works for two very different audiences at once: influencers who live in a visual, social space, and business decision-makers who care about ROI.

items.title: Logo & visual identity
items.text: We created a new logo and visual system using a high-contrast green–black palette and confident layouts that instantly read as tech-forward, creative, and social.

items.title: Bold visual direction
items.text: We positioned TheyTalk as an AI layer that turns influencer marketing from guesswork into a focused, performance-driven channel.

items.title: Visual communication system
items.text: We combined logo, color, type and graphic elements into a compact visual platform that can stretch across product UI, web presence, pitch decks, and social content.

items.title: UX/UI design for platform
items.text: We designed UX and UI for the key platform pages. Defined the initial user flow together with the founders. Brought the new look and feel directly into the product.

items.title: Usable brand guidelines
items.text: We handed over mini-guidelines and a clear structure for typography, color and component usage, so the start-up team can grow the system without breaking it.

sections.title: How We Used AI (And How We Did Not)
sections.content: AI helped with research, visual exploration and generating supporting media assets, especially for speed and volume.The actual identity, art direction and UX decisions came from the design team. AI acted as a production helper, not a creative director.

sections.title: The Result
sections.content: TheyTalk now has a bold visual identity and a set of platform screens that tell the story in seconds. This is influencer marketing with a brain. The logo and design system give the founders a recognisable face for the product in investor rooms and early sales conversations. The project proves that even under start-up constraints, you can build a brand that works.
